rationale: Tests definition of infertility and the 6-month threshold for women over 35 — a key clinical fact introduced in the Clinical Presentation block
Tests understanding that semen analysis is part of the initial evaluation and should be ordered early — the Systematic Investigation block emphasises both partners simultaneously
Tests the shared fundamental principle of all tubal patency tests — introducing a substance under pressure — covered in the Anatomy and Governing Principles block
Tests appropriate management when tubal disease is confirmed — laparoscopy is the gold standard and allows simultaneous treatment, covered in the Surgical Options block
Tests selection of the correct first-line ovulation induction agent for a WHO Group II (PCOS) patient — the Regimens, Monitoring, and Selection block covers letrozole vs clomiphene for PCOS
Tests understanding that OHSS is graded and mild cases can be managed conservatively — the Management of Complications block introduces OHSS severity classification
Tests the key distinction that ICSI — not standard IVF — is specifically designed to overcome severe male factor infertility by injecting a single sperm into the oocyte
Tests knowledge of the ART (Regulation of Assisted Reproductive Technology) Act 2021 — the regulation and clinical decision-making block covers ART governance in India
Tests correct application of Rotterdam 2003 criteria — any 2 of 3 criteria required; a common exam trap is requiring all 3
Tests understanding that PCOS carries long-term metabolic risks including endometrial cancer from unopposed oestrogen — the Long-Term Complications block covers this
Tests categorisation of causes of hyperandrogenism by source — ovarian vs adrenal vs idiopathic — the Causes block introduces a systematic source-based approach
Tests understanding that combined oral contraceptive pills reduce androgen levels via both pituitary suppression and SHBG increase — key mechanism from the Management block
